• Lurkers and/or /v/all users (non-subscribers) unable to influence communities they visit or post to?

The last two points above can be merged into one to create a concern that Putt has still not addressed, and which is much more complex than most concerns raised so far. Specifically, the idea of a long con.

With the upcoming Votes system, what is to stop 1000 redditors -- maybe even paid shills -- from coming over the Voat right now, and each of them posting five comments a day in 15 of the biggest subverses on Voat. That's 75 comments a day (which isn't too much) per account.

If, a year from now, there is an important Vote (a referendum / Outcome Vote let's say) in any of those biggest 15 subverses, then all 1000 accounts will likely be able to get past any restrictions imposed on the referendum (account age, CCP in subverse, number of comments in the past month, etc.) and thus those 1000 accounts may be able to overwhelm the native goats in that referendum, and vote one of their own into power.

One might argue that "Well, they've been actively using the subverses for a year, why shouldn't their vote count in that way?" but of course the problem is these are malevolent agents we're talking about -- the kind who would take over major Voat subverses and could, between them all, get a stranglehold on Voat's largest communities.

It is for this reason that I think, at the very least, @system subverses should not have referenda at all. They can still have polls, which don't automatically produce an outcome, but no outcome votes. I think the safest thing to do with @system subverses would be to rely on Putt's judgment, rather than potentially giving power to power-hungry groups. This may slow down action time, however. What could be done is the @system subverse could hold a poll and see what the results are, and Putt could use the results of that non-outcome vote to make his decision, or he could disregard it. A big part of the reason this feature is being implemented is to give the community the power to moderate itself, and make it so we have to rely less on Putt, but I think with respect to Voat's biggest subverses it is important we retain that final check and balance. It would ensure the integrity of Voat's larger community is maintained -- purely immune to long cons of any kind.

If this were done, it would mean referenda could only be used in communities that are fairly large but not @system subverses (since Putt has said very small subverses will not be able to use referenda also).

If my above suggestion is not considered, then I think some other means of preventing long cons from malicious groups must be devised.

If anyone has other concerns about the feature, let me know and I'll add it to this list. I'd like to have a complete map of concerns both addressed and as yet unaddressed.
